title: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
description: 1 astronomical unit ÷ the speed of light: the Sun you see is 8 minutes old.

shots.title: The Sun, and the question
shots.say: You have never seen the Sun as it is right now. Its light takes time to get here.

shots.title: Sun to Earth: 149.6 million km = 1 AU
shots.say: On average, the Sun is about 149.6 million kilometers away. Astronomers call that one astronomical unit.

shots.title: Speed of light: 299,792 km/s
shots.say: Light in a vacuum covers about 299,792 kilometers every second. That is about 7.5 laps around the equator.

shots.title: A light pulse crosses 1 AU in 8 min 19 s
shots.say: Divide the distance by the speed, and you get about 499 seconds. That is 8 minutes and 19 seconds.

shots.title: Moon 1.3 s, Sun 8 min 19 s, Neptune about 4 h
shots.say: Light from the Moon takes about 1.3 seconds. From the Sun to Neptune, it takes about 4 hours and 10 minutes.

shots.title: The sunlight on your face left 8 minutes ago
shots.say: So when sunlight warms your face, you're feeling light that set out about 8 minutes ago.

shots.title: End card
shots.say: Light is quick, but the universe is so much bigger.
